rules.name: A reversal is expansion met with opposite expansion at meaningful liquidity
rules.setupAnchor: Price sweeps an external liquidity reference such as a previous-day high or low, previous-week high or low, session high or low, or the latest marked swing extreme
rules.confirmationTrigger: The sweep is followed by opposite-direction displacement that closes back through the swept reference or back inside the source range
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: The first protected swing that forms in the new direction becomes the structural invalidation for reversal execution and later continuation
rules.invalidationCondition: Price keeps expanding through the swept external reference without the opposite-direction close or later fails to hold the first new protected swing
rules.targetLogic: First objective is previous-day equilibrium or nearby opposing liquidity, then the opposite side of the range or next external pool
exceptions: A sweep alone is not enough without opposite-side expansion or closure
If the move only pauses and then resumes in the original direction, treat it as a retracement failure instead of a reversal
pineInputsNeeded: close location relative to swept reference
machineChecks: Detect a sweep beyond one of the tracked external liquidity references
Tag the reversal to the highest-timeframe breached reference when multiple tracked levels overlap on the same move
Require a close back through the swept reference or back inside the source range after the sweep

rules.name: Reversal confirmation is stacked from wick, liquidity sweep, CISD, and close behavior
rules.setupAnchor: Price sweeps a tracked previous-day, previous-week, session, or swing reference and leaves a higher-timeframe rejection wick or V-shape
rules.confirmationTrigger: A lower-timeframe CISD closes through the candle series that made the extreme while price also closes back through the swept reference
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: The lower-timeframe shift that confirms the wick becomes the structural reference for executing or invalidating the reversal thesis
rules.invalidationCondition: The wick midpoint is disrespected under wick logic, CISD never forms, or price cannot close back through the swept reference
rules.targetLogic: Use the confirmed shift to frame entry timing and then target the next opposing liquidity pool
exceptions: Wicks inside consolidation are less reliable than wicks that sweep external liquidity
Below the four-hour chart, reversal framing gets noisier and should be filtered by higher-timeframe bias
pineInputsNeeded: wick respect or disrespect state from wick logic
machineChecks: Read midpoint respect or disrespect from the wick-logic topic instead of redefining wick tolerance locally
Detect a close through the candle series that created the extreme
Require the same move to close back through the swept reference

rules.name: If candle two fails, candle three closure can still confirm the reversal
rules.setupAnchor: Price reaches an already-mapped fair value gap, imbalance, or order-block style zone and candle two does not produce the reversal closure
rules.confirmationTrigger: Candle three closes over the body of candle two in bullish context or below the body in bearish context without sweeping candle two's extreme
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: A swing is only valid when the mapped zone is paired with a valid closure, so candle three closure can still validate the reversal swing
rules.invalidationCondition: Candle three also fails to close through candle two's body or the move sweeps candle two's extreme without the required close
rules.targetLogic: Once valid, anticipate candle four expansion and refine entry around candle three equilibrium on the lower timeframe
exceptions: Candle three closure can signal either reversal or continuation depending on context, so higher-timeframe framing remains mandatory
The zone must already be mapped by the higher or intermediate timeframe context rather than discovered only after candle three prints
pineInputsNeeded: candle two open high low close
candle three open high low close
machineChecks: Detect whether candle two failed to produce the reversal close
Detect whether candle three closes through candle two's body in the required direction
Reject the fallback if candle three sweeps candle two's extreme before the required close
Gate the fallback behind an already-mapped aligned zone rather than discovering a new zone on candle three

rules.name: The first-pass reversal sequence is sweep, reclaim, CISD, and gap-backed entry
rules.setupAnchor: Price enters London or New York and sweeps liquidity at a mapped higher-timeframe reversal anchor
rules.confirmationTrigger: The first-pass sequence requires a sweep or purge, a reclaim or inversion back through the move into the extreme, a CISD through the candle series that made the extreme, and an entry location such as a fair value gap, candle-three equilibrium, or breaker-style retest after the shift
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: Later-stage confirmations should sit behind a newly formed opposite-direction protected swing or equivalent structural shift
rules.invalidationCondition: The sweep never reclaims the level, CISD never forms after the reclaim, or the new protected swing fails before continuation develops
rules.targetLogic: Earlier entries improve R but carry less confirmation; later entries sacrifice price for cleaner structural validation
exceptions: The first-pass codable subset ends at reclaim, CISD, and entry location; breaker blocks are optional later refinement rather than a required first release
Time-of-day filtering matters, especially for index reversals around New York AM

Require a sweep to be followed by a reclaim back through the extreme area before looking for CISD
Require CISD after the reclaim and before enabling any entry location
Allow selectable entry families such as fair value gap, candle-three equilibrium, or breaker-style retest after the shift
